GodTask.ts is mutable: its fields are plain `public` and `complete()`, `updateTitle()` and `addTag()` change the object in place. The two models also disagree on structure. Task has `createdAt`, while GodTask has `priority` and `tags`. Both define the same validity rule (`isValid(): boolean { return this.title.length > 0; }`), so the invariant lives in two places and can drift. Neither class uses the other or a shared abstraction. Only Task is used elsewhere (CreateTaskUseCase, ITaskRepository, InMemoryTaskRepository), so GodTask runs alongside it as a second entity. GodTask also mixes in concerns that are not domain logic: serialization (`serialize()` via JSON.stringify), presentation (`toString()`) and copying (`clone()`).
